Tax Administration Jamaica 

Practice Note 

Permitted Accounting  
Period 

This Practice Note is intended only as a general guide and must be read in 
conjunction with the relevant legislation. It contains the Authority’s interpretation 
of the law as it stood at the date of this publication along with any associated 
practices, procedures and instructions. 

Under Section 12 (2) of the Tax Administration Jamaica Act, 2013 a Practice Note 
is binding on the Commissioner General and all officers of the Authority until it is 
revoked. However, taxpayers are reminded that the publication of a Practice Note 
does not affect their right of objection and appeal or their right of access to the 
Revenue Court on points concerning their own liability to Income Tax. 

Comments and suggestions for the improvement of issued Practice Notes and 
suggestions for future Practice Notes are always welcome. 

July 1, 2019   

                                  Commissioner General

This Practice Note provides guidance with respect to the application in accordance with Section 
6 of the Income Tax Act of Jamaica for approval for a Permitted Accounting Period to end on 
some date other than December 31st.   

The examples in this Practice Note are strictly for purposes of illustrating the issues and 
concerns identified by Tax Administration Jamaica in making decisions on such approvals. 

All references herein are to the Income Tax Act unless otherwise indicated.

I. Glossary of Terms and Abbreviations 

1.  The following list defines various terms and abbreviations used in this Practice Note. 

Accounting Period 

An accounting period, in bookkeeping, is the period with reference to 
which accounting books of any entity are prepared. It is the period for 
which books are balanced and the financial statements are prepared. 
Generally, the accounting period consists of 12 months. 

Basis Period 

“Basis Period” is the accounting period in a particular Year of Assessment 
for which a taxpayer is required to compute his or its taxable profit for 
Income Tax purposes and tax liability. 

It is usually the accounting period that coincides with the Year of 
Assessment but it can also be a Permitted Accounting Period. 

Body corporate 

A person, association, or group of persons legally incorporated 

CG 

Commissioner General of Tax Administration Jamaica 

Chargeable Income   Section 2 of the Income Tax Act - "chargeable income" means the 

Default period 

aggregate amount of income of any person from all sources remaining 
after allowing the appropriate deductions and exemptions under this 
Act. 

The default period for tax purposes is the "year of assessment", i.e. the 
period of twelve months commencing on the 1st day of January in each 
year. 

Emoluments 

Includes, in relation to any office or employment of profit, items as 
defined in Section 2 of the ITA.  

First Effective Year 

This is the first year of the newly requested accounting period. It is the 
first taxable year for which a change in annual accounting period is 
effective.  

Financial Year 

A financial year is a period of twelve months, used by business, and other 
organizations in order to calculate their budgets, profits, and losses. It is 
any annual period at the end of which a firm's accounts are closed and 
financial reports are prepared. Section 2 of the CA stipulates that, in 

1 

 
 
 
 
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

relation to a body corporate, this is the period in respect of which any 
profit and loss account of the body corporate, laid before it in general 
meeting is made up, whether that period is a year or not. 

Any compensation, payments or benefits due to or received by any 
person in the furtherance of a trade, business or profession. Section 2 of 
the Income Tax Act defines "trade" to include every trade, manufacture, 
adventure or concern in the nature of trade.  The term “Profession has 
not been defined in the Act but its literal meaning as defined by many 
scholars and accountancy bodies identifies it as a vocation, or a job 
requiring  some thought, skill and special knowledge like that of 
accountant, lawyer, doctor, engineer, architect etc. So profession refers 
to those activities where the livelihood is earned by the persons through 
their intellectual or manual skill. Section 5 of the Income Tax Act of 
Jamaica gives more meaning to “profits or gains” which are chargeable 
to income tax. 

Income Tax Act of Jamaica 

Application Form for a Permitted Accounting Period 

Permitted accounting period, in relation to any person, means the 
accounting period, other than a 12-month period ending December 31st, 
in respect of which the gains or profits of any trade, profession or 
business carried on or exercised by that person are permitted or 
required to be computed pursuant to Sections 6 (2), 6 (3), 5, or 6 (4) of 
the ITA. 

"Permitted accounting terminal date", in relation to any permitted 
accounting period, means the ending date of the period. 

As stated in Section 2 of the ITA "person" means any individual and also 
any body of persons.

II. Purpose 

2.  The purpose of this document is to provide guidance to the public in general on the 

interpretation of the provisions of Sections 6 (2), 6(3), & 6(4) of the Income Tax Act of 
Jamaica and more specifically, guidance on the application and approval for a permitted 
accounting period, i.e. an accounting date terminating on a date other than 31st day of 
December.  

3 

 
 
 
 
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

3.  This PN sets out the factors to be taken into consideration when making a request to the 
CG to allow an alternative accounting period, other than one ending December 31st. 

4.  This PN seeks to ensure that the decision on whether to allow an entity to adopt a 

permitted accounting period involves balancing the interests of that entity with that of 
the Revenue thereby ensuring an efficiently administered income tax system.  

III. Objectives 

This Practice Note is: 

5.  To provide guidance to persons affected by the law and to the officers of TAJ.  This is in 
accordance with Section 12 of the Tax Administration Jamaica Act, 2013 which states 
that the CG may issue Practice Notes setting out the interpretation and procedures for 
the application of the Law. 

6.  To promote and achieve consistency in the administration of the Laws relating to 
domestic tax. It is also to be used to streamline the processing of applications for 
approval of a permitted accounting period to improve efficiency and service to 
taxpayers. 

7.  To provide taxpayers with a degree of certainty regarding specific policies, guidelines 

and procedures on the application and approval for a change of accounting year end to 
some date other than 31st day of December, i.e. a permitted accounting period.  

8.  To provide taxpayers with a degree of certainty regarding specific policies, guidelines 

and procedures in instances where approval was granted by the CG: 

(a)  For a change in accounting year to some date other than 31st day of December 

and the taxpayer makes a subsequent request for another change.  

(b) For a change in accounting year to some date other than 31st day of December 
and the taxpayer has now made a subsequent request to revert to the default 
year ending 31st day of December.  

9.  To provide taxpayers with a degree of certainty regarding specific policies, guidelines 

and procedures in instances where no approval was granted by the CG: 

(a)  For a change in accounting year to some date other than 31st day of December. 

(b) For a change in accounting year to some date other than 31st day of December 

4 

 
 
 
 
 
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

and the taxpayer has now made a subsequent request to revert to the default 
year ending 31st day of December.  

IV. Scope & Background  

10. In administering the law relating to a permitted accounting period; this Practice Note 

sets out the interpretation and administrative rules of the CG in respect to Section 6 of 
the ITA governing the change in accounting period to a permitted accounting period. It 
also provides TAJ’s position with respect to the submission of an application for 
approval of the change.  

11. The requirement for the approval of any planned change in an entity’s accounting 

period for Income Tax purposes has long been in existence and is in accordance with the 
law. However there have been no recommended rules and guidelines for instructing the 
taxpayer on how to secure this approval for a permitted accounting period. 

12. Where a date other than the default period is being used and the CG is not aware of 

this, the taxpayer’s income tax account on TAJ’s database will not reflect this change. As 
such, the CG intends to ensure that the RAiS is properly configured to evaluate the 
expectations of each taxpayer who is required to file returns.  

13. Therefore, if an existing taxpayer wishes to change their accounting period from the 
default period to any other 12 month period or a new taxpayer wishes to adopt an 
accounting period other than the default period, the net income shall, with the approval 
of the CG, be computed on the basis of such new proposed accounting period. 

V. Need for a policy guideline 

14. There was no fixed period within which to make the request to secure the approval of 
the CG. The ITA is silent on a required timeframe within which to make a request for 
securing the CG’s approval for a permitted accounting period. 

15. A permitted accounting period affects the deadlines/due dates for paying income tax 

and filing of an Income Tax Return. 

16. Section 6 (2) of the ITA establishes that a person can make a request for permission for 
their year to end on a date other than the 31st day of December.  However, there is no 

5 

 
 
 
 
 
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

provision for instances where an individual has multiple sources of income, inclusive of 
emoluments. 

17. In considering a request to change to a permitted accounting period, the CG will look at 
relevant matters, consistent with the statutory responsibilities under Section 6 of the 
ITA so as to maintain the integrity of the tax system. 

VI. Statutory requirements for a permitted accounting period 

18. Sections 6(2), 6(3) & 6(4) of the ITA generally provides that a taxpayer who wishes to 
change its accounting period and use a permitted accounting period must obtain the 
approval of the CG  

19.  Section 6 (2) provides that, in conjunction with subsection (1), where the CG is satisfied 
that any person usually makes up the accounts of his trade, profession or business to 
some date other than the 31st day of December he may permit the gains or profits of 
that trade, profession or business to be computed upon the income for the period of 
twelve months terminating on that date in the year of assessment to which the 
accounts of that trade, profession or business are usually made up.  

20. Section 6 (3) of  the ITA provides that where a person commencing to carry on a trade, 
profession or business satisfies the CG that he/she intends to make up the accounts to 
a date other than the 31st day of December, the CG may grant permission under 
subsection (2). 

21. Where permission is granted as per paragraph 15 above and under circumstances where 

(a)  the first accounts of the trade, profession or business have not yet been drawn 

up; and  

(b) the first accounts of a trade, profession or business covers a period which 

exceeds twelve months,  

the income of the period shall be treated for this purpose as being apportioned at an 
even rate between the twelve months terminating on the date to which the accounts 
are made up and the remainder of the period.   

22. Under Section 6 (4) of the ITA where a person departs from his permitted accounting 

terminal date, i.e.  his ending date,  

(a)  The new permitted accounting period will be determined by the CG identifying:  

(i)  The Y/A in which the departure occurs and 

6 

 
 
 
 
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

(ii)  The Y/A immediately following the departure period 

(b) The permitted accounting period determined by the CG for the Y/A in which the 

departure occurred may include any interval between the end of the old 
accounting period and the commencement date of the new permitted 
accounting period. 

(c)  The terminal date of the new permitted accounting period as determined by the 
CG will be regarded as the permitted accounting terminal date of this person 
until another permitted accounting period has been requested in accordance 
with the provisions of the legislation and the guidelines of this PN. 

23. After a determination of the taxpayer’s permitted accounting period has been made by 
the CG in accordance with section 6 (4), if the taxpayer subsequently chooses to change 
his permitted accounting period, the taxpayer must first seek approval from the CG. Any 
further applications for change will be assessed in accordance with the criteria set out in 
section 6(2) & (3) of the Income Tax Act. 

VII. Commissioner’s Powers 

24. Under PART VID, Section 17O of the Revenue Administration (Amendment) Act, 2013 

the CG  

(i)   “May establish an electronic communication system (in this section referred to as 

the "system”) including provision for any or all of the following operations- 

(a)  filing of electronic documents with the Commissioner General;  
(b) service or issue of electronic documents by the Commissioner 
(c)  ………………………….. 

(ii)  For the purposes of subsection (1), the Commissioner General may make rules 

providing for any or all of the following 

(a)  ……………………………… 
(b) the type of documents that may be sent through the system including the 

format and manner of sending them, ………………………… 

(c)  the format for, and the content of, information that is to be included in 

documents sent through the system; 

(d) ……………………………………….. 
(f)  the determination of when a document that is filed through use of the 

system is received by the Commissioner General; 

7 

 
 
 
 
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

(g)  …………………. 
(h) any other matter for the better administration or operation of the system. 

(iii) An electronic document that is communicated by means of the system is deemed to 
have been received by the person to whom it is communicated, unless the contrary 
is shown.” 

25. Section 18A of the Revenue Administration (Amendment) Act, 2013  states that 
“Without limiting the powers of the Minister under Section 19, the Commissioner 
General may, by order published in the Gazette prescribe forms of returns and other 
forms that the Commissioner General considers to be necessary for the various purposes 
of this Act, whether for general use or use in any particular case or for the use of any 
particular person or group of persons” 

VIII. Reasons for requesting a permitted accounting period 

26. Taxpayers will require a permitted accounting period based on sound business reasons. 
The CG’s view is that the following non-exhaustive list of reasons could constitute 
"sound business reasons": 

(i) A person may change accounting year in order to consolidate the filings of their 

Income Tax return if they are operating in a group environment or have to make 
international filings; 

(ii) A person changes its accounting period to end on the same date as that of its 

parent or associated company; 

(iii) A person changes its accounting period to ease financial reporting requirements 

under various legislations and to various reporting entities; 

(iv) A person may wish to adopt a change to its accounting period when they can 

demonstrate that the nature of their business makes a December 31st year end 
impractical; or their circumstances have changed significantly and they should be 
permitted to change to some date other than December 31st.  

(v) To avoid busy trading periods. Entities might wish to avoid having to prepare 

accounts or conduct stock takes during their busy periods; 

(vi)  A person may wish to adopt a permitted accounting period for business entities 

8 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

with a close working relationship, where they share a common business and/or 
management accounting system or central administration structure and one of 
those entities already has a permitted accounting period. This category includes 
joint ventures that want to adopt an accounting period common with that of its 
partner; 

(vii) Persons who were granted a permitted accounting period or who had, without 
prior approval, used a period other than the default period, may subsequently 
want to revert to the default filing period. 

However, neither the personal convenience of the taxpayer, nor the saving or deferment of 
income taxes will be considered a "sound business reason".  

IX. Who will be allowed a permitted accounting period? 

27. Section 6(2) of the ITA provides for any person to request an approval for a permitted 

accounting period. 

28. Section 2 of the ITA defines “person” as any individual and also as any body of persons. 
"Body of persons" means any body politic, corporate or collegiate, and any company, 
fraternity, fellowship and society of persons, whether corporate or not corporate. 

29. Bodies corporate, regardless of business type may be permitted to change their 

accounting period to end on some date other than December 31st. Generally, individuals 
must adopt the calendar year as their default period; however, Section 6 of the ITA does 
not preclude them from requesting a change. (see paragraph 30).  

30. For individuals, approval to use an accounting period ending with a date other than 

December 31st must include the full emoluments earned for the calendar year in which 
the permitted accounting period ends. The CG will not allow apportionment of 
emoluments when accounting for the profits and gains. In determining the liability, the 
income tax threshold relevant to that Y/A must be used. Take note that emoluments 
normally accrue on a monthly basis and must be accounted for in a Y/A.  (see 
Illustration 1)  

9 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

X. Taxpayers’ Obligations 

31. For income tax purposes, a taxpayer who proposes to change their accounting year end 

shall, before using the new period, comply with the provisions of the ITA relating to a 
permitted accounting period by securing the approval of the CG to change the 
accounting year end on some date other than the 31st day of December. 

For newly registered businesses the CG has used his discretionary powers to allow new 
registrants to identify and adopt the period so identified as its permitted accounting 
period. (see paragraph 32) 

32. Any newly registered business seeking to use an accounting period ending on a date 
other than 31st day of December must ensure that at the time of registration and 
application this is made known to the person completing the registration process. This 
is to ensure that at the point of registration the proposed accounting year is properly 
noted in RAiS and the requisite tax accounts can be accurately created.  

Therefore, the first Income Tax Return (i.e. by submission of the estimated or final 
return, whichever comes first) for that newly registered business with a year-end other 
that 31st day of December; will be the default application for permission for that 
person. The CG will require that this return, and all subsequent returns, must be filed 
online via TAJ’s Tax Portal. 

However, there will be instances where the CG will request that a newly registered 
business must make a formal application online for permission to use a year-end other 
that 31st day of December.  (see paragraphs 45 - 49). 

XI. Procedures for granting approval for a permitted 

accounting period 

33. The CG, has exercised his powers under Sections 17O & 18A of the Revenue 

Administration (Amendment) Act, 2013, and has instructed that, effective September 1, 
2019 it will be mandatory that the request for a permitted accounting period be made 
on-line via TAJ’s Tax Portal using the prescribed form designed for that purpose. 

10 

 
 
 
 
 
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

34. In the interim, all persons requesting a change are required to complete a PAP01 
application form (See Exhibit 1) which must be prepared by the taxpayer or their 
representative. In addition, an attached written explanation of the reason for the 
request to change the accounting period will also be required. If this explanation is not 
included, the processing of the application will be delayed until the information is 
provided. This form must be downloaded from TAJ’s website, www.jamaicatax.gov.jm 

35. All requests must be directed to1  

The Commissioner General 
Tax Administration Jamaica 
Technical Specialist Unit 
10th Floor, Office Centre Building 
12 Ocean Boulevard 
Kingston 

36. If the tax returns are already overdue at the date of application, the taxpayer will not be 

approved for a change in accounting period.  

37. When agreeing to a change to an accounting period, the CG will only agree to a 

permitted accounting period with a year-end that is the last calendar day of a month. 
No other permitted accounting period terminal date will be accommodated. 

38. A permitted accounting period will remain in effect until the entity applies for, and is 

granted permission to adopt another permitted accounting period.  

39. Where permission was previously granted for an entity to use an accounting period 

ending on some date other than December 31st and the entity now wishes to revert to a 
period ending December 31st it will be required to submit a PAP01 application form 
seeking permission to do so. 

40. Where a decision was taken not to allow a permitted accounting period, the CG will 

provide the taxpayer with a full explanation of the reasons. While there are no objection 
rights against a decision not to allow a permitted accounting period, the taxpayer may 
seek to have the CG review his decision and provide the CG with reasons why it is felt 
that the decision so made was incorrect. 

1 For manual applications submitted up to August 31, 2019. As of September 1, 2019, the request must be done online. 

11 

 
 
 
 
                                                           
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

XII. When to file an application for a permitted accounting 

period 

41. The request for approval for a permitted accounting period must be done within the 

required submission time. The request must be submitted not less than 60 working days 
before the beginning of the proposed new accounting period. 

(a)  A taxpayer must submit such an application to TAJ no later than 60 working days 

before the start of the proposed new accounting period. However, TAJ 
recommends that the application be submitted as early as possible to provide 
TAJ with adequate time to respond to the request prior to the proposed new 
accounting period and the due date of the taxpayer’s return for the first effective 
year. 

(b) Any taxpayer whose application is submitted less than 60 working days before 

the start of the proposed new accounting period may have their request denied. 
The taxpayer may be asked to continue using the existing accounting period and 
make a resubmission for a permitted accounting period in keeping with the 
required time frame given in this PN.  

(c)  However, the CG may consider an application that has been filed after the 

required submission time. If special circumstances exist, a taxpayer may also 
request an extension of time to submit their application giving reasonable cause 
for such delay. (see paragraphs 42- 44).  

Notwithstanding, no extension will be given that will cause a return to be filed late.  

XIII. Applications submitted after the specified time  

42. Any application submitted less than 60 working days before the start of the proposed 
new accounting period may be considered as a timely submission if the taxpayer 
establishes that he/she acted reasonably and in good faith, giving a reasonable cause for 
the delay in submitting the application and that granting approval will not prejudice the 
interest of the Revenue.  

12 

 
 
 
 
 
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

43. The CG may consider unusual and compelling circumstances or any such occurrence 

which prevents a taxpayer from applying for a permitted accounting period within the 
specified time. These can include, but not limited to: 

-  Serious illness or accident; and serious emotional or mental distress, such as 

death in the immediate family; 

-  Natural disasters, such as a flood, fire, hurricane. earthquake; 
-  Civil disturbances or disruptions in services, such as a riot, incursion; 

44. If a taxpayer’s circumstances do not fall within the situations described above but the 

CG is satisfied with the explanation the taxpayer provides, the CG may consider such an 
application to be timely. 

XIV. Adoption of a permitted accounting period by new 

registrant 

45. Given the powers under Section 6 (2) & (3) of the ITA the CG will permit a newly 

registered business, to adopt a permitted accounting period ending on a date other than 
31st day of December by filing its first Income Tax Return using that period, which then 
becomes its default application for permission. However, this permission is under the 
premise that the first set of accounts is not more than twelve (12) months. (see 
paragraph 46 below) 

46. Notwithstanding Section 6(3), where the first set of accounts of the newly registered 
business is for a period in excess of 12 months the taxpayer must apply online for 
approval to use some date other 31st day of December by completing the PAP01.  

47. After a newly registered business has adopted an accounting year, it must continue to 
use that accounting year when computing taxable income and filing its returns online 
for all subsequent years; unless it obtains approval from the CG to make a subsequent 
change to its year end to some other date. 

13 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

XV. Changing a permitted accounting period to another 

permitted accounting period 

48. Section 6 (4)(a) states that where a taxpayer has departed from its permitted accounting 
terminal date the CG may require the taxpayer to use as the relevant accounting period 
for that Y/A in which the departure occurred, and the following year, such periods as the 
CG  may determine. The period determined by the CG, in relation to the departure, may 
include any interval between the permitted accounting date of the old accounting 
period and the commencement of the new accounting period. (see Illustration 2) 

49. When there is a change in permitted accounting period there will be profits of a basis 
period of more or less than twenty-four (24) months to be assessed in two years of 
assessment. If the change is to a date later in the year than the original permitted 
accounting date there will be more than 24 months profits to be assessed in the Y/A in 
which the departure took place and the next succeeding year. The law provides that the 
excess may be included in the year in which the departure took place. The year in which 
the departure took place is the Y/A in which falls the date to which an account of the old 
permitted accounting period should have been made up to or the date to which an 
account on the new permitted accounting date is made up, whichever is earlier. (see 
Illustration 3 & 4) 

50. Where the change is to a date earlier than the original permitted accounting date then 

there will be less than 24 months profits to be assessed in the Y/A in which the 
departure took place and the next succeeding year. The law provides that the permitted 
accounting period for the year in which the departure took place and the next 
succeeding year shall be such period as the CG may determine.  

51. Normally such determination will be that the permitted accounting period for the year 
in which the departure took place will be the period between the permitted accounting 
terminal date of the old permitted accounting period and the commencement of the 
new permitted accounting period; i.e. the departure year is for a period of less than 12 
months and that the accounting period for the next succeeding year will be 12 months 
ending on the new permitted accounting date. (see Illustration 5) 

14 

 
 
 
 
 
 PN-PAP 01-2019                                                                                              

XVI. How often can a person apply? 

52. A person will generally not be allowed to apply for more than one change within a 

specified period, with exceptions. (see paragraph 54). The specified period is considered 
to be a period of five years within which a person to whom approval was granted for a 
permitted accounting period is not allowed to make a new application.  

53. However, a request for permitted accounting period can be made more than once 

within the specified period but the taxpayer is obligated to ensure that the provisions as 
laid out in Section 6 of the ITA regarding the approval is adhered to. 

54. In the CG’s assessment of the application for another change within a specified period 
the CG will look at whether or not there are extenuating circumstances requiring the 
change, such as: 

-  Aligning the accounting period with that of a subsidiary or its parent company; 
-  Where the companies are operating in a group environment; 
-  Where the business is in liquidation. 

Take note, it is not possible to set out all the circumstances in which an approval may or

XVIII. How to treat an unauthorized permitted accounting 

period 

61. Despite the strictness of the provisions in Section 6 of the ITA, the CG has taken the 

decision that any unauthorized change made by a taxpayer prior to the publication of 
this PN ( i.e. prior to July 1, 2019) will be accepted as their permitted accounting period 
(see Illustration 6).   

62. Therefore, all unauthorized changes will be ratified by the CG and the taxpayer will be 

formally advised of this decision. (see Exhibit 3). However, for any unauthorized change 
which occurs after July 1,2019  the CG will enforce the provisions of  Section 6 of the ITA 
as well as the procedures laid out in paragraphs 33– 40 of this PN. 

63. Individuals with multiple sources of income inclusive of emoluments who have been 
using some date other than December 31st must now conform to the instructions   in 
paragraph 30.  

64. To the extent that an individual had apportioned his emoluments in keeping with the 

accounting period that was in use, that individual must now account for the remaining 
emoluments for that year of assessment on his next return. However that individual will 
only be entitled to the unutilized PAYE credit, if any, from the prior calendar year, in 
addition to the PAYE credit from the emoluments earned in the next year of assessment. 
(see Illustration 7).   

XIX. Capital Allowance Treatment 

65. Where a permitted accounting period results in a period greater than or less than 

twelve (12) months, the capital allowance to be claimed is dependent on whether the 
asset is in use at the end of the basis period.

66. Where a taxpayer previously received the necessary approval as outlined in Section 6 of

request to change to some other date. At that time, the procedures laid out in 
paragraphs 33– 40 of this PN and Section 6 (4) (b) of the ITA must be followed.

To determine where the excess profits should be included you need to determine the 
year of departure. The following rule will be applied in determining the year in which the 
departure took place: This is the earlier of the Y/A in which falls: 

(i)  The date to which the old permitted accounting period should have been made 

up to OR  

(ii)  The date to which the new permitted accounting date is made up.

permitted accounting date would now end December 2016.  Therefore the year of 
departure is 2016. The succeeding Y/A is 2017 where the taxpayer will return to a 12-

December 2017 and continue thereafter to make up accounts for the 12 months ending 
31st day of December.

Illustration 6: No prior approvals. Change requested to synchronize with parent 

VI.  A parent company has been using an unapproved permitted accounting period ending 
September, which they have been using more than 10 years ago. It has acquired 
controlling shares in another company. The new subsidiary has been using an 
unauthorized accounting period ending March. The parent company has made a formal 
request to change the accounting period of the subsidiary company to synchronize with 
the year-end being used by them. 

TAJ’s response:  
Both companies made unauthorized changes and have been using accounting year-ends 
other than 31st day of December. The parent company’s request to change to a new 
accounting period for the subsidiary was carefully considered by the CG. The decision 
was taken that at this time the change was necessary. The CG will ratify the 
unauthorised change made by the parent when it used a September year-end and also 
approve the request for a permitted accounting period for the subsidiary given the 
following circumstances:  

  The parent is synchronizing the year-end of its subsidiary to correspond with its 

own 

  The Revenue is not disadvantaged by the change requested. The change to 
September by the subsidiary has not affected the due date of the return. 

Given the length of time in which the unauthorized changes have been continuing 
without early detection by TAJ, in good faith, the CG has enforced the provision of 
Section 6(2) of the ITA.
